lastReleaseMessage: v1.4.1: the closing pass before the indefinite pause drops the retired run targets and records what stays open

barRaise.topFinding: Every medium and high finding carried into this run is closed in code and verified: the save failure now reports instead of printing a silent success, the prune has a real test, the cost readout says it is an estimate, the readiness check warns on an old runtime, and an unmatched stream line renders rather than vanishing. The proof-of-life receipt the previous run asked for exists. What it proves is thin: one connectivity check, produced to close that finding, against thirteen locked decisions and eight versioned burn-downs on a tool that reached version one on 2026-06-23. Receipts dated 2026-06-18 are also still on disk past a ninety-day retention the code claims to enforce.

Closed as moot rather than fixed. The project is paused under D81 and this finding is a question about where to spend, which the stall has answered. Kane at 23:19 on 2026-09-22: complete the open work on the stalled projects and stop building new work for them. A live hazard on a system that still has users stays open and gets fixed, because stalling development does not stop a defect reaching somebody. An improvement to work that is not happening does not. Nothing is deleted: this entry is the record, and the finding comes back the day the project does.

Closed on evidence rather than as unrecoverable, because this one could be recovered. docs/DESIGN.md records it as D-012: runs/ is retained for ninety days, then pruned (compliance-data-steward-02, 2026-09-04), which means the finding was the retention policy and it was implemented and promoted to a locked decision that day. Verified live this session: RUN_RETENTION_DAYS is 90, pruneOldRuns runs once at boot and daily after, and driving it against real fixtures removed both .jsonl receipts when every file was eligible, spared a non-receipt in the same folder, and kept a fresh receipt at the ninety-day window. The live runs/ folder holds nine receipts, oldest 2026-07-16, inside the window.

The comment in server.mjs named indefinite retention against the shipped ninety-day prune, which makes a receipt read as permanent when it is not. It now names RUN_RETENTION_DAYS, the boot-and-daily prune, and the window over which GET /runs/:file can still serve it. The finding also asked for direct confirmation that the prune reaches eligible files, which is done: against real fixtures it removed both .jsonl receipts when every file was eligible, spared a notes.txt in the same folder, and kept a fresh receipt at ninety days. The prune keys on birthtime, so a receipt ages from when it was written, which is right for a file that is never modified after it is created.
